lines.speaker: A
lines.text: When students plan to improve their study habits, they often set goals that are too ambitious. A plan to study for three hours every night may work for a few days, but it can be difficult to maintain. A more practical approach is to start with a short activity linked to an existing routine. For example, review five words after breakfast. The familiar routine acts as a reminder. Once the activity becomes easy, increase it gradually. Keeping a simple record can also help. The purpose of the record is not to punish yourself for missing a day, but to notice patterns and make realistic adjustments.

questions.prompt: What problem is mentioned at the beginning?
questions.why: 开头指出目标过于宏大而难以坚持。

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of keeping a record?
questions.why: 最后一句强调观察规律并合理调整。

lines.speaker: A

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. We initially recruited participants through technology companies, but that produced a sample with very similar backgrounds.

lines.text: So the issue was representativeness rather than the number of responses?

lines.speaker: B

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Only slightly. We are keeping the core questions so that the results remain comparable. The additional recruitment will take another six weeks.

questions.prompt: Why was the project delayed?

questions.prompt: Why retain the core questions?
questions.why: 保留核心问题是为了使结果可比。

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Urban trees are often promoted as a simple solution to rising temperatures. Their leaves provide shade, while evaporation from the leaf surface cools the surrounding air. However, the benefits are not distributed equally. Wealthier neighbourhoods frequently have denser tree cover than areas with lower incomes. Planting programmes therefore need to consider social equity as well as total numbers. Another challenge is maintenance. A young tree placed in a narrow pavement may struggle if its roots lack space or its soil dries out. Successful programmes budget for years of care, rather than treating planting day as the end of the project.

questions.prompt: What inequality does the speaker identify?
options: Tree cover differs across income groups.
All trees need the same care.
questions.why: 高收入社区通常树冠覆盖更密集。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker recommend?
questions.why: 种植后仍需多年养护预算。

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Today we are considering a common error in interpreting research: assuming that because two things occur together, one causes the other. Imagine a study finds that people who visit museums report higher levels of wellbeing. It may be tempting to conclude that museum visits directly improve mental health. Yet visitors may also have more free time or stronger social networks, and these factors could influence wellbeing. Researchers call such factors confounding variables. Randomised experiments can reduce some of these problems, but they are not always practical or ethical. In observational research, transparency about limitations is therefore essential. A cautious conclusion is often more scientifically valuable than a dramatic one.

questions.prompt: What is the lecture mainly about?
questions.why: 通过博物馆案例说明相关不能直接推出因果。

questions.prompt: What are free time and social networks examples of?
questions.why: 这些额外因素可能影响幸福感，属于混杂变量。

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: This lecture introduces urban wetlands. These habitats serve several functions that are sometimes overlooked in city planning. First, wetland vegetation slows the movement of water, reducing the risk of flooding after heavy rain. Second, the soil and plants can trap pollutants, although this does not remove the need to control pollution at its source. Wetlands also provide a habitat for birds and insects. When creating a wetland, designers must pay attention to water depth. A variety of depths supports a wider range of species. Long-term monitoring is necessary, because a site that looks attractive may not yet be functioning as a healthy ecosystem.

questions.prompt: Wetlands reduce the risk of ______. (ONE WORD ONLY)
questions.why: 植被减缓水流，降低洪水风险。

questions.prompt: Designers should vary water ______. (ONE WORD ONLY)
questions.why: 不同水深支持更广泛的物种。

questions.prompt: Long-term ______ is needed. (ONE WORD ONLY)
questions.why: 最后指出要进行长期监测。

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Urban environments offer an interesting setting for studying animal behaviour. Consider birds that live near busy roads. Traffic noise is strongest at lower frequencies, which can interfere with communication. Some birds respond by singing at a higher pitch. Others shift the timing of their songs to quieter periods. These changes may help individuals find mates or defend territory. However, a change in behaviour is not necessarily a genetic adaptation. An individual bird may adjust its song within its lifetime. To establish evolutionary change, researchers would need evidence that relevant traits are inherited across generations.

options: To compete with low-frequency traffic noise.
To reduce the number of songs.
questions.why: 交通低频噪声干扰交流，升高音调可避开干扰。

questions.prompt: What distinction does the speaker emphasise?
questions.why: 个体一生中的行为调整不等于跨代遗传的演化。

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: During my final year, I investigated how students choose sources for academic writing. I interviewed twelve volunteers and asked them to explain why they trusted particular websites. One finding was that a professional appearance often influenced trust more than the author's qualifications. The project was small, so I would not claim that the results apply to all students. If I continued the research, I would recruit participants from different disciplines and compare interviews with observations of their actual search behaviour.

questions.prompt: What limitation does the speaker acknowledge?
options: The project had no research question.
questions.why: 只有十二名志愿者，因此不把结果推广到全部学生。

questions.prompt: What would the speaker add in future research?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: When evaluating an educational intervention, an improvement in test scores is useful evidence, but it is not sufficient on its own. Students may improve simply because they have become familiar with the test. A comparison group can help researchers separate this practice effect from the impact of the intervention. It is also important to examine whether the improvement lasts. A test administered immediately after a course may produce different results from one taken three months later. For this reason, my proposed study includes both a comparison group and a delayed assessment.

questions.prompt: Why is a comparison group useful?
questions.why: 对照组帮助区分熟悉测试所带来的练习效应。

questions.prompt: Why include a delayed assessment?
questions.why: 延后测试检验学习提升能否持续。
